title: Circumstances Surrounding Leasing of Ridout Road Properties by Ministers' Families
what_it_is: Circumstances Surrounding Leasing of Ridout Road Properties by Ministers' Families

sections.label: Ridout Road ministerial lease questions
sections.summary: Questions to the Prime Minister on privileged information, a press conference, and the reviewer of the Ridout Road tenancies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister (a) how will the Government assure the public that the Minister for Law and the Minister for Foreign Affairs were not in receipt of any privileged information pertaining to the lease of 26 and 31 Ridout Road respectively; and (b) whether there are any rules, conventions or policies to ensure that Cabinet Ministers do not take advantage of privileged information received in the course of their official or non-official duties in regard to the lease of Government properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister what are the Government's reasons for not calling a press conference in May 2023 to address the public allegations in regard to the lease of 26 and 31 Ridout Road to the Minister for Law and the Minister for Foreign Affairs respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister why is the Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security tasked to review Minister K Shanmugam's tenancy of 26 Ridout Road and Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's tenancy of 31 Ridout Road, rather than an individual from another branch of Government, such as a Supreme Court Judge.

sections.label: SLA guide rent for Ridout Road
sections.summary: Question to the Minister for Law on the guide rent set by SLA for the leases of 26 and 31 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law what was the guide rent set by SLA for the lease of 26 and 31 Ridout Road when they were leased out to the Minister for Foreign Affairs and the Minister for Law respectively.

sections.label: Black and white bungalow questions
sections.summary: Questions to the Minister for Law on redevelopment, audits, bidding, conflicts of interest, and maintenance costs for black and white bungalows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law whether the Government has plans to redevelop more of the land that are currently occupied by black and white colonial bungalows for more productive uses like public housing, industry or commerce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) whether the bidding process of black and white bungalows managed by SLA is audited by the Auditor-General's Office annually; (b) if not, in which year was the latest audit conducted; (c) what sampling methodology was used for the latest audit conducted; and (d) whether bids by Government officials, Members of Parliament and related parties are always included as part of this sample.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) how long was the bidding open for 26 Ridout Road after Minister Shanmugam's bid was received as compared with the normal procedure for such bids; and (b) whether there is any prescribed process for declaring any related party transactions or conflicts of interests when bidding and how was that process observed for 26 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) how are maintenance and upgrading costs for black and white bungalows owned by SLA divided between tenant and SLA; and (b) what are the annual costs of maintenance and upgrading borne by SLA at 26 and 31 Ridout Road respectively from 2013 to 2022, inclusive of both years.
